rv.q: But the conceptual framing that makes it special is also a limitation.
Audiences will lap up the melodies, singing and storyline.
As had the rest of the very young West End audience with an average age of, I'd say, 27, who stood and cheered this production of The Last Five Years to the rafters.
The Last Five Years really is a slice of perfection.
It’s disappointing as The Last Five Years has a lot of individually strong elements, but it never feels like it adds up to more than the sum of its parts.

cn.t: Brown's clever concept and melodic score charm in this bittersweet two-hander, though some flaws persist. Strong performances and emotional storytelling win over audiences despite structural limitations.
